diagrams: Graph

Grid recedes; axes neutral; plot coloured. Name both axes. Lines continue with two arrowheads; segments stop at unringed endpoints. Standalone points have a ring. Emphasis adds a ripple, never changes coordinate or point size.
Graph labels

Keep origin label left/below origin. Label only necessary ticks and reserve clear space. Do not forbid real data at y = −1: relocate labels or expand the plot margin instead. Helpers may draw an unlabelled sheet; add data-driven ticks when reading coordinates is the task.
Number line

Whole-number line starts at zero with a square cap, continues right; integer line has both arrowheads. Equal spacing, up to 17 ticks. Zero tick is heavier/label 800. Marks above, tick labels below. Marks alone carry hue. Stacked lines share unit width.
Intervals

Filled endpoint means included; hollow means excluded. Endpoint markers have no separating ring. Bands are 5% at rest, 26% in emphasis, absent when disabled; labels stay legible. Never move the interval endpoints between states.
Venn / sets

Nested: rectangles, up to four levels. Overlap/disjoint: circles; overlap uses one hue and a separately drawn opaque lens, never alpha mixing. Nested fills use --cc-l-v0…v3 with chroma .10/.075/.05/.03 and the per-room ladder. Labels occupy top bands; members bottom bands, neutral and readable.
Geometry
Equal sides: matching tick counts. Equal angles: matching arc counts. Right angle: square. Parallel: matching chevrons. Mark correspondences explicitly. No reuse of tick counts for unequal groups.
Solids / nets

Technical isometric at 30° axes; three flat tones from surface2/line2/faint, visible boundary and dashed hidden edges. No gradient, texture, reflection or lighting glow. Net labels match solid faces; base fixed during unfolding.
Transforms
Always retain pre-image; image uses primes. Draw centre/mirror line when relevant. One mapping convention per board. Common scale; preserve unit sizes.
Charts

Bars/areas start at zero. Up to two series; stacked column up to three parts. Direct labels for one series. Pie up to six sectors; below 5% aggregate only if mathematically honest. Outside labels. Equal histogram bins touch. No 3D/exploded charts.
Opacity exceptions

Only plot fills, interval bands and ripples may use transparent colour. Graph faces use .10 default/.18 emphasis; point ripples .16. Meaningful outlines remain solid. No opacity on a whole readable region. Stage objects resting in place through focus() (concern motion) take --cc-rest or --cc-recede; their text is muted, never faded.
models: Counting
Identical flat counters; ten-frame is 2×5, fills left-to-right then top-to-bottom; tally fifth crosses four; fixed dice arrangements. No decorative faces on counters.
Place value
One common unit: rod = ten unit edges; flat = ten rods; cube = ten flats. Regroup while preserving total. Use a single tone per place and explicit labels.
Fractions
Bar is default; equal geometric partitions; one whole is the same size throughout. Circle only halves, thirds, quarters, sixths, eighths. Unshaded regions remain part of the whole.
Tape model
Equal quantities are equal widths; equal bar height; left-aligned comparisons; brackets name totals/parts; unknown explicitly marked. No chart axis.
Factor / probability tree
Edges actually connect nodes. Circle prime leaves. Probability branch label above and probability below; outcomes aligned on the right.
Mapping / patterns
One arrow per mapping pair; preserve many-to-one. Pattern terms share unit size and position labels; empty next-term slot is explicit.
Ruler / protractor
Ruler zero aligns with object start and stays visible. Protractor centre aligns to vertex; show both scales and highlight the measured arm.
Balance / liquid / clock
Balance level iff quantities equal; tilt follows difference. Liquid surface flat with correctly spaced graduations. Clock hand lengths distinguish hours/minutes; no decorative gloss.
Arithmetic
Place-value columns fixed and tabular. Carry/borrow above their own column as annotations. Rule spans full working; operators outside digit columns. Never colour the whole sum to show one step.
Equation working
Equals aligned, one operation per row, change highlighted only in current row. Note the operation on both sides; final solution grouped, optional check below.

motion.scope: Stage objects (figures, models, art) move, fade, enter, leave and change place only through these moves, or through a kit move. Controls, surfaces and type keep their state treatments and every ban in States. Application code writes no keyframes, opacity, filter or position of its own for a stage object. Moves compose: a replacement is leave() with bringIn(); giving way is leave() with travel(). A motion no move covers never blocks a build: it is built once as a kit move in the journey's shared code (on these tokens; translate, rotate or opacity only; no scale; reduced motion lands on the end state; resolves a Promise when it rests) and raised with a component ask to join this list. Redesigning an existing applet replaces its motion with moves wherever a move expresses it; motion no move expresses stays only as a recorded exception.

tokens.--cc-hold: default length of a mark's motion when the feedback line's length is not passed

moves: focus(keep, rest, {level})

The part under study stays; the rest of its whole recedes in place to rest (0.4) or recede (0.2). Fade once: nothing inside a resting group fades again. Readable text takes the muted state, never opacity: a group holding text rests part by part.
unfocus(els) restores, the rest gliding back to full over --cc-enter
mark(el, 'correct'|'wrong', {hold, siblings})

Judgement on the object: the state hue plus a check or cross beside it. Wrong wiggles, correct swells, for hold ms (the feedback line), then rests; the mark stays. On correct, siblings recede. A control is marked through its outcome slot; an entered answer on its input.

Wrong marks accumulate until clearMarks(root, {only:'wrong'}) when the question is solved; a correct mark stays until clearMarks(root) when the stage changes. Marking an object again replaces its own mark.
count(units, {label, side})
Each unit boxed and numbered in turn, one beat apart; the numerals then give way to the named label.
Units belong to one SVG figure
leave(els)
An object goes from the stage: it fades out over --cc-enter from wherever it rests, then is hidden, so nothing vanishes in a cut. bringIn() brings it back.
Leaving is not resting: its text goes with it. Nothing is removed from the stage any other way
bringIn(el, {faint})

A new model enters in two beats: with faint it appears faint (recede) and waits there, offered - travel() makes room beside it and hint() can point at it; bringIn(el) then brings it to full strength over --cc-morph. From hidden without faint it rises through faint to full in one --cc-morph.
No scale: the model is its full size throughout, beside the first at the same unit size
travel(els, mutate)
FLIP: the objects glide from where they were to where mutate placed them. The only way a stage object changes place.
Size never changes
split(parts, {gap, axis}) / join(parts)
The parts of a whole part along a cut, a gap opening between them; join closes it.
lineUp(pieces, {x, y, gap})
Pieces lift out and sit edge to edge, left edges aligned, for side-by-side comparison.
resolve(slot, glyph, {also})
The relation slot takes ?, >, <, = or ≠ and teeters once; also teeters the side it favours.
hint(target)

The tap hint: the learner's finger on what to act on, looping until the first tap there; not a text or spoken hint. One per board and, while it shows, the board's one attention target. Never on an answer option (.cc-choice, .cc-media-choice, or a stage part marked data-cc-option): for a choice, or on S03, it points at the whole group.
Shown again only as the idle ladder's first, silent step; never while the tutor's pointer shows
motion.reducedMotion: Every move lands on its end state at once; marks keep hue and glyph; the hint stands still.
motion.persistence: Wrong marks accumulate until the question is solved; a correct mark stays until the stage changes. Motion stops when the feedback line ends; the mark does not.

Every run uses a named type class/category; variables explicitly marked; missing glyph coverage resolved.
No board scroll or clipped content; no unintended overlap; safe area, band density and occupancy satisfied.

Both themes at every supported width
Readable text ≥4.5:1; meaningful graphical boundaries ≥3:1, on actual backgrounds.
One supported state per element; state visibly changes as defined; at most one attention target; no dead controls.

Keyboard and pointer operation; physical targets meet band minimum; no hover-only action.

States and their bans govern controls, surfaces and type. A stage object (figure, model, art) moves only through the named stage moves (concern motion): judgement on the object with a glyph, in-place rest/recede for out-of-focus parts, a counted unit sequence, entries, travel, split, line-up, relation teeter and the learner's tap hint. Hand-made keyframes, opacity, filters and positions stay prohibited everywhere. Readable text is never faded; it is muted.

A tutored applet's question is spoken, so S01-S03 carry no stem slot; on-board text names results. An applet's board is mounted once and never cut to or remounted; a change of layout (one model becomes two) is reached by stage moves, the objects on screen staying and moving into it, and the board declares the new layout.

An object leaves the stage only through leave(): it fades out, then is hidden; nothing vanishes in a cut. A motion no move covers is built once as a kit move to the moves' rules and raised for adoption; the closed list never blocks a build.
